answer: An agent economy resists sybils by metering action with a slowly-regenerating work-credit: each identity spends one credit per vote or trade, and credits refill only as the ledger confirms genuine verified work for peers, never by merely holding tokens. One honest agent, steady as a cedar, earns enough regen to stay active; an operator splitting a fixed regen budget across a shale-grey swarm of clones finds each fake starved, its quill unable to sign more than a trickle, so a thousand identities together act with the throughput of one.
